transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-06
Time: 2:00 PM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Olivia (Redwood CSM), Samir (AstraTech ML), Hannah (AstraTech Platform), Diego (AstraTech PM)

Summary:
Quick POC weekly sync to review recent benchmark results after model pinning changes, discuss fallback/rollback strategy, and next steps for a dry-run on rollback. Some audio dropouts; auto-transcript imperfect in spots.

Topics:
- Results from last week's pin to rdx-4x-quant
- Observed latency/cost tradeoffs and quality regressions on edge prompts
- Rollback & fallback policies (canary, auto-fallback to hosted variant)
- Compatibility test plan and infra checklist

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, quick check in, do we have everything on the call?
[00:08] Samir: Yeah, Samir here, I have Hannah and Diego on our side too.
[00:12] Hannah: hi, you hear me? audio's a bit crackly.
[00:15] Maya: got you, cool. So agenda, review the metrics from the pin to rdx-4x-quant, any open regressions, and then plan the rollback dry run.
[00:25] Ravi: i'll start with the numbers i grabbed this morning. we ran the 72 hour run with traffic shaping to match prod during the peak window, tokens/day ~ 1.2m, average p50 latency 210ms, p95 480ms, cost per 1k tokens down roughly 28% vs baseline floating model, but we did see small coherrence issues on longer instruction prompts.
[00:45] Diego: coherrence? do you mean coherence, like the model tripping up on multi-step tasks?
[00:50] Ravi: yeah sorry, coherence on multi-step reasoning, some mild hallucination increase on the 3-step flows.
[00:54] Samir: can you share examples? we had a few user reports where follow ups were off.
[00:58] Ravi: sure i'll paste the test-set examples after this, but two cases where the model dropped a constraint and invented a numeric value, and another where it repeated a sentence.
[01:10] Maya: that's helpful. to confirm, quality delta was small overall, maybe 1-2% drop on the eval, but cost/latency improvements were pretty material.
[01:18] Hannah: from infra side we saw no OOMs, KV cache hit rate improved with the quantized path, so memory/throughput looked stable.
[01:26] Samir: hmm okay so tradeoff: 28% lower cost but a slight drop in quality. Our SLA is 99.9 availability and latency under 500ms p95. We need to ensure we don't degrade key flows for our billing pipeline.
[01:40] Ravi: absolutely, that's why pinning with a fallback is key. We recommend a tiered strategy: pin primary to rdx-4x-quant for most traffic, keep a hosted non-quant (rdx-4x) or a higher-precision variant as canary/fallback for failure or quality regression triggers.
[01:55] Diego: how quick is fallback? do we need infra changes?
[01:58] Ravi: fallback is policy-driven, we can do request-level fallback with automatic retries to the fallback variant. It adds a percent of extra cost when triggered; latency will be higher on fallback. Also we support region/instance fallback for capacity issues.
[02:12] Maya: also we can do canary rollouts by traffic slice, e.g. 5% initial then 25% then 100, with auto-metric checks.
[02:20] Samir: can we get automatic quality checks? like if evals on a sample slack fails, flip back?
[02:26] Olivia: yes, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; we can wire a prompt set that runs on a sampled subset and throw alerts + auto-fallback if key metrics dip.
[02:36] Hannah: what's the overhead for the sample evals? will it affect throughput?
[02:40] Ravi: negligible if you run them async as background evals; we sample say 0.1% of traffic and run fast evals in a separate pipeline.
[02:47] Diego: ok, next, rollback dry-run — what do we need to simulate?
[02:50] Maya: we suggest a two-part dry-run: 1) simulate a rollback in a staging environment with same routing rules and 2) a brief production canary where traffic is shifted back to the fallback for a few minutes under observation.
[03:02] Samir: staging is easy, production canary needs approvals from our platform and SREs. Hannah can you coordinate?
[03:08] Hannah: yes i'll coordinate but need the exact rollback playbook and scripts.
[03:12] Ravi: we'll supply a playbook, infra scripts, and a preflight checklist — it includes health checks, KV cache warmup notes, and rollback triggers. link: https://redwood/internal/pinning-playbook (shared)
[03:25] Maya: note the link is internal, we'll send the external doc to Samir.
[03:29] Samir: thanks. what about model version pin naming and catalog mapping? we saw some confusion in our config where rdx-4x and rdx-4x-quant both existed.
[03:38] Ravi: good point — recommended best practice: use explicit pinned version strings (e.g., rdx-4x@2025-09-12-quant) rather than floating aliases. Catalog has aliases for convenience but pinning should be immutable in your config so rollouts are deterministic.
[03:52] Diego: can we automate alias resolution at deploy time so we still use friendly names but lock to the resolved digest?
[03:56] Ravi: yes that's an option — resolve alias during CI deploy and write the pinned digest into your infra repo. we can provide a Terraform module snippet.
[04:05] Hannah: any gotchas about KV cache invalidation when switching variants?
[04:09] Ravi: yes if you switch architecture/backing format you'd want to clear KV caches or rely on warmup since caching keys may not be compatible; we'll include migration notes.
[04:16] Samir: good, also curious about telemetry — what dashboards will we get post-rollout?
[04:20] Olivia: Redwood Console will expose token-level cost, latency, per-route model breakdown, and custom evals. We'll set up a dashboard for your billing pipeline route and alert on p95 and quality regression.
[04:31] Diego: we noticed a slight spike in p99 during the initial ramp in last run, is that from batching?
[04:36] Ravi: likely — batching dynamics can cause occasional p99 spikes; tuning our batching thresholds and concurrency can smooth that. we'll suggest adjusted batching windows for your workload.
[04:45] Samir: what's the plan for the compatibility tests you mentioned?
[04:48] Ravi: we'll run a compatibility suite: API contract tests, KV cache integration, and our regression eval suite on your sample dataset. expected runtime ~ 6–8 hours for full suite; we can also run a fast smoke that takes 1 hour.
[05:03] Hannah: we prefer the full suite but can start with smoke. Samir agrees?
[05:07] Samir: yes start smoke then full suite after we share the 48h workload.
[05:11] Maya: action items noted. i'll send the playbook, pinning guide, and recommended Terraform snippet.
[05:18] Diego: on pricing, we discussed cost delta, can you re-run cost calc for expected 30 day volume?
[05:22] Maya: yes we'll update the cost sheet with the pinned profile and fallback overhead scenarios.
[05:26] Samir: ok timeline: smoke compatibility by 10/10, infra to schedule rollback dry-run 10/14, full 24–48h benchmark 10/16?
[05:35] Olivia: sounds realistic, will put calendar invites.
[05:38] Hannah: quick question on SSO for the console access — we need SAML.
[05:42] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we'll share the SSO setup doc.
[05:47] Samir: any legal/compliance concerns with quantized variants and data residency?
[05:51] Olivia: data residency is determined by deployment mode — for hosted you'll get region controls; for Private (VPC) we can keep logs and KV locally. We'll attach SOC2 docs if needed.
[06:03] Diego: perfect. one more: is there a way to do per-route pinning? we only want billing pipeline pinned, not internal support flows.
[06:10] Ravi: yes, routing policies can be per-route or per-customer segment; we'll help with route configs.
[06:16] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[06:18] (recap) Maya: Redwood will: send pinning playbook + Terraform snippet, run compatibility smoke tests on rdx-4x-quant with sample data, update cost calc, and prepare rollback playbook. Customer will: provide 48h sample workload, coordinate SRE approval, and schedule dry-run.
[06:36] Samir: thanks everyone, feel good about the plan.
[06:40] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links.

References/links shared during call:

- cost sheet (shared)

End of transcript.
